property_summary: On any winning play, the winner's balance increases by exactly pot_before - FEE_AMOUNT (the 1-wei fee goes to the bank); the mutant pays the full pot, so for some winning (timestamp, difficulty, player) input the winner's received amount is 1 wei too large.

For any admissible (timestamp, difficulty), calling play with the exact 10-wei ticket from a player whose receive() accepts any payment up to pot-FEE (9 wei) never reverts; the mutant pays the full pot (10 wei), which the picky player rejects, so the winning play reverts for inputs where the pseudo-random outcome is 0.

For any block timestamp/difficulty, a 10-wei play from a player whose receive() accepts at most 9 wei never reverts (a win pays out pot-1 = 9 wei), but the mutant pays the full 10-wei pot on a win and the picky player rejects it, reverting.
Whenever a winning round completes (pot reset to 0), the bank must have received exactly FEE_AMOUNT; the mutant omits the fee transfer, so on a win the bank's balance stays unchanged.

On any admissible play, whenever a winning round resets the pot to 0 the bank must have received exactly FEE_AMOUNT (1 wei) during that call; the mutant omits the fee transfer, so on a winning round the pot is 0 while the bank's balance is unchanged.

Whenever a play ends in a winning round (pot reset to 0), the bank's balance must have increased by exactly FEE_AMOUNT during that call; the mutant deletes the fee transfer, so on a win the bank's balance rises by pot-FEE instead (e.g. 9 instead of 1 when the bank itself plays).

Whenever a successful play ends in a winning round (pot reset to 0), the contract's ether balance must drop by exactly the pre-call pot (bank receives FEE_AMOUNT, winner receives pot-FEE_AMOUNT); the mutant omits the bank fee so the balance only drops by pot-FEE_AMOUNT, violating the rule.

After one successful (non-reverting) play, any subsequent play must also succeed: in P a won play pays out from an adequately funded pot, while M's deleted pot update makes the payout arithmetic revert.
